"Stock" trainings?

A call from an organization looking for trainings got me re-thinking - after the cursory introduction with the L&D manager was a question, which went something like "what kind of trainings do you have for Gen Z?"

As always, I requested to probe further any particular pain-points or requirements, answers being stonewalled as "normal Gen Z issues." Upon persistent probing, an issue that was mentioned - frequent job changes by Gen Z - leading to more queries from my side, trying to understand their work pattern, any recent incidents, anything that they had to share.

"I will get back to you after my vacation, thank you!" the L&D manager hung up 😊 

If trainings were to be over-the-counter prescriptions, why even do them? one can watch videos online or probably put the money to better use.

Training, technical or people skills should be backed by the right intention, probably a knowledge gap or skill gap or a change in process or a new hire or an acquisition or a change of mindset - this list could be endless and any responsible organization in-charge should be able to pinpoint the need.

Unless the trainer "diagnoses," the training is not going to meet the expectations or objectives intended. 

Why should trainers even bother to probe and analyze?
1. Training done without analyses has also been appreciated - it is momentary, might not last beyond a week. Once the organization realizes their objectives were not met, the buck is passed to the trainer!
2. Trainer was awesome, but audience could not connect dots - again analyses was not done, and no matter how knowledgeable or skillful the trainer was the objectives were not met - again the trainer is the fallguy!

Make any more permutation/combinations of the situation, the equation is simple - the trainer takes the final responsibility - NOTHING else MATTERS!

Do your analyses the right way, take time, be sure and then the results will be awesome!

Remember even your family doctor takes time to diagnose - its just the flu, just a paracetamol will do!
